sources.entry: AnonAddy - Email forwarding service for creating aliases. (Source Code) MIT PHP/Docker

summary.one_liner: Source code for addy.io, a self-hostable anonymous email forwarding service that creates aliases which forward to your real inbox.
summary.what_it_does: The README is largely an FAQ for the hosted addy.io service and doubles as a feature description for the open-source PHP application. Users create email aliases (shared-domain, random character/word, or standard on-the-fly aliases) that forward to verified recipient addresses. Replies and sends from aliases are supported, with the real address hidden. It supports custom domains via TXT/MX records, multiple usernames, optional GPG/OpenPGP encryption of forwarded mail with a user-supplied public key, bandwidth and rate limits, and 2FA. Self-hosting requires Postfix, PHP 8.2+, Redis, MariaDB/MySQL, Nginx and Rspamd, plus DNS (MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and reverse DNS. The README also notes that a Docker image is maintained separately at github.com/anonaddy/docker.
use_cases: hide real email address from spam
per-site email addresses for tracking data breaches
how_to_run: Set up a server with Postfix (3.0.0+), plus postfix-mysql and postfix-pcre
Install PHP 8.2+ with php-mailparse, and php-gnupg and php-imagick if needed
Install Redis 7.x+, MariaDB/MySQL, Nginx and Rspamd
Configure DNS: MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, reverse DNS and a FQDN hostname
Follow the self-hosting instructions file referenced in the README
Alternatively use the Docker image at github.com/anonaddy/docker (maintained separately)
notable: Shared-domain, random character/word and standard on-the-fly aliases, with per-user usernames to compartmentalise aliases
Bring-your-own GPG/OpenPGP public key to encrypt forwarded mail, including attachments and protected subject headers
Replies and sends from aliases with the sender's real address stripped, and public keys removed from outgoing mail
Spam filtering via Rspamd, DNS blacklist checks, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, and PTR checks
Official mobile apps and browser extension are built by others and linked from the FAQ
caveats: Self-hosting requires substantial server administration knowledge (Postfix, PHP, DNS, reverse DNS) and port 25 open
Several paid-plan limits apply to the hosted service (e.g. alias creation rate, bandwidth, custom domains, additional usernames)
Forwarded mail may still land in spam initially, depending on the recipient provider
